pairs.subject: engine-host-contract
pairs.evidence: core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:28 This core turns pen messages into an annotation document a TV shell feeds and reads; a search of core/ for JobExecutor, ModuleLoader, HostHooks, microtask and macrotask found none, so there is no language engine evaluating source through host hooks, job queues or a module loader.

techniques.evidence: core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Protocol.kt:7 The published surface is the phone-to-TV pen protocol, not a language specification's host-hook table.
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:8 The shell carries effects out; there are no promise jobs, so no null or blocking executor is chosen.
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/History.kt:45 Undo applies an operation to the annotation list immediately; nothing is a job held outside a traced guest heap.
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:34 The shell applies pen messages and a frame loop only reads the document; no promise, timer, native or cleanup queue is drained.
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Protocol.kt:167 Inbound text is decoded as one pen message; there is no referrer, specifier or filesystem root.

core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:7 Callers pass times in. Pairing stores one forward-only Long (see at line 54) for a PIN cooldown; there is no wall-clock or guest date/timer seam to split.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path applies only to a language engine that evaluates source, but the subject name engine-host-contract does not say so, so a host-driven library can look in scope until use_when is read.
